summary: Documented M3-S02 (Classic acknowledgement + escalation email templates and folder — EmailFolder:case_intake, EmailTemplate:case_intake/Case_Acknowledgement, EmailTemplate:case_intake/Case_Escalated_To_Tier2 — plus sender-identity-note.md) after step-tester marked it tested. Re-rendered PLAN.md/CLARIFICATIONS.md before and after the status transition. Wrote four Section 2 workbook rows (CWB-LAYOUT-003..006 in workbook/02-page-layouts-and-lightning-pages.md, since the step's type `ui` is the same type M1-S02 carries and Step 4's map names email templates for that section) and two Other Configuration rows (CWB-OTHER-019 package.xml, CWB-OTHER-020 deploy-order.md); minted two new requirement ids (REQ-032 the customer acknowledgement, REQ-033 the Tier 2 escalation handover notice), continuing from the highest existing (REQ-031), and wrote their traceability.md Matrix rows, a requirement-id-derivation pair, a 'What M3-S02 rests on' section citing Q22/Q63/Q68 on REQ-032 and Q63/Q88 on REQ-033, a Coverage section and a Linter-result section; appended four decisions (D-M3S02-01..04 — the ungrounded description ceiling, the inferred intra-request deploy order, the deliberate no-WorkflowAlert omission, and — most load-bearing — the Q22-vs-answers-key sender-identity divergence, recorded as an M3 milestone-gate decision that M3-S04's senderEmail must not pre-empt, recommending a non-routing OWEA and citing admin/email-to-case-configuration's mail-loop gotcha) and five open items for the planner (O-M3S02-01 the Q22/answers-key contradiction as a clarification-record defect, O-M3S02-02 the deliverability checker's assertion-free exit 0, O-M3S02-03 deploy-order.md undeclared in outputs[] on both M3-S02 and M3-S01 with amend-step ruled out for already-documented steps, O-M3S02-04 the stale unfiled$public/ template prefix two consumer skills would hand M3-S04/M4-S04 plus the Q88-vs-REQ-033 notification-mechanism distinction, O-M3S02-05 a check_rtm.py skill-depth gap on EmailFolder-qualified naming). Compiled the step's one manual test (B06) into two UAT cases (TC-M3S02-01 positive, TC-M3S02-02 negative — added so the checker's unconditional per-requirement negative-case rule was satisfied honestly rather than skipped) and two Given/When/Then criteria (AC-032.1, AC-032.2), staged in the session scratchpad and linted clean by both check_uat_case.py and check_ac_format.py. Set the step's status to documented via build_plan.py. No other M3 step was running concurrently with this pass.
confidence_rationale: Every one of the step's seven declared outputs plus the one undeclared deploy-order.md produced a workbook row (six rows total, two of them each covering two files that are one component), every new traceability row carries a real source_req_id freshly minted from requirement.md and an answered clarification (Q22 for REQ-032, requirement.md L15-16 plus Q63 for REQ-033), and both rows name a verification cell that states what passed and what no exit code in this step asserts. Re-running this pass would replace the same six workbook rows and two traceability rows rather than duplicate them (all keyed). Not MEDIUM: the step's type (`ui`) is a named row in Step 4's map (not a fallthrough to Other Configuration), no artefact needed judgment to place in a section, and neither requirement id was inferred from an ambiguous field — REQ-032/REQ-033 read directly off requirement.md's own acknowledgement and escalation lines. The Q22-vs-answers-key divergence and the check_rtm.py false-orphan WARN are both genuine open items, but Step 11's rubric scores the documentation task, not the underlying build's unresolved substantive questions — both are recorded exactly where they belong (a gate decision and a skill-depth open item) rather than either hidden or left to silently degrade a row's accuracy, which is the same treatment M3-S01's HIGH call gave its own six open decisions and four open items.

process_observations.observation: check_uat_case.py enforces an unconditional per-requirement negative-case rule (independent of check_ac_format.py's narrower rule-type-marker trigger). Rather than skip it, a second, genuinely grounded negative case (TC-M3S02-02 / AC-032.2, reusing the tester's own grep-for-@ evidence) was added so both linters passed honestly instead of one being silently under-satisfied.

Both new templates' merge-field bodies were independently re-confirmed to contain no email address (grep -c @ = 0 on both, matching the tester's own tests/M3-S02/summary.md evidence) before being cited as the negative case's oracle, rather than trusting the prior run's prose.

The Q22-vs-answers-key sender-identity divergence this step's own artefacts recorded is now a decisions.md entry (D-M3S02-04) rather than only a note buried in sender-identity-note.md — but it remains unresolved, and it is load-bearing: M3-S04, the very next routing step, is the one that actually sets senderEmail.

check_rtm.py's file-to-component deriver has no folder-qualification rule for EmailFolder-nested EmailTemplate files, so its orphan report flags two correctly-covered rows as uncovered purely from a key-derivation mismatch — a false positive that would mislead a reader who trusts the WARN count without reading the orphan report.

The ten-position deploy-order sequence in agents/build-doc-keeper/AGENT.md Step 5 has no slot named for EmailFolder/EmailTemplate, the same gap M3-S01 already recorded for `validation` and workbook/01-objects-and-fields.md recorded for `BusinessProcess` — a third step type now missing from the same list.

Whether Q88's queue-level notification default and REQ-033's case-level escalation handover notice are meant to compose, substitute for each other, or run fully independently is not stated anywhere in the plan; this run recorded them as distinct mechanisms on the more conservative reading, but a human at the M3/M4 gate may intend otherwise.
M3-S02 is documented; M3-S03 and M3-S04 are the next pending M3 steps, and M3-S04 in particular is where decisions.md D-M3S02-04's sender-identity gate decision actually gets exercised.
process_observations.followup_reason: M3-S03 and M3-S04 are both pending and M3-S04 depends on this step; advancing the milestone requires them built, tested and documented next, with D-M3S02-04 read before M3-S04's senderEmail is written.

process_observations.observation: check_rtm.py's missing EmailFolder-qualification logic (O-M3S02-05) is a repeated, uninstrumented manual correction every future email-template step will need a human or a doc-keeper run to explain away.
process_observations.followup_reason: recorded here as a skill-depth candidate rather than acted on, because deepening a checker script is out of this agent's scope and belongs to the skill's own maintenance path, not a workbook compile.
